solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: a verb: to put an end to, as a rumour is quashed
the whisky distilled in Scotland

annotation.surface: Someone suggests pausing a journey to have a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a pub stop, but 'stop' is a verb here: to scotch something is to quash it.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning to put an end to, as a rumour is quashed, and the whisky distilled in Scotland.

entries.clue: General shot right for photographic device (8)

indicators.note: shot as in wrecked or ruined, so the letters of GENERAL are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
R = right, the standard abbreviation, added to the mix

annotation.surface: A general is photographed, or shot, from the right-hand side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'General shot' paints a military figure gunned down or photographed; 'General' is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the darkroom machine projects a negative onto paper to make a bigger print.

entries.clue: Go early and take legs over arm? (4,3,3)

blocks.note: to act too soon, like a sprinter leaving before the starting pistol
literally leap (take your legs) over a firearm (an arm)

annotation.surface: A gymnast is told to start early and vault legs over an arm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arm' reads as a limb, but it is a weapon, a gun; the question mark flags that the second half is a literal, whimsical reading of the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from athletics, leaving before the starting pistol, so acting prematurely; the second reading takes the phrase literally.

blocks.note: to win something is to obtain it
E = energy, as in E = mc²

annotation.surface: Someone is told to get an energy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' reads as one sporty product, but the two words split: energy gives E and drink is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: fermented grape juice is one kind of drink.

indicators.note: drunk as in staggering and muddled, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Advice not to save a drunk who must fend for himself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the person who needs rescuing, a noun; it is the instruction to jumble the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: with no companion or chaperone means on your own.

definitions.note: Amen is an interjection affirming what is said; 'without a doubt' is used the same way, as an emphatic 'truly'.

blocks.note: taken as it stands
a crew is a team of men

annotation.surface: A crew described as certain, beyond question.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Amen to that' is said to agree emphatically, which is why an exclamation of certainty can define it.
annotation.definitionFit: A liturgical word meaning 'truly' or 'so be it', used in speech as emphatic agreement, just as 'without a doubt!' is.

blocks.note: under someone's influence is to be in their power
a sect is the kind of group ruled by a Svengali, a manipulative leader

annotation.surface: A sycophant is under the spell of a manipulative mentor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' suggests a toady, which fits the surface; it is a creepy-crawly. Svengali, the hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, stands for anyone controlling followers, as a cult leader controls a sect.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal sense: bugs and beetles are creepy-crawlies, so a crawler is a fair name for one.

entries.clue: All The King’s Men (in black and white?) (5,3)

definitions.text: All The King’s Men (in black and white?)

blocks.note: the pieces that serve the king on a chessboard
the two colours of the pieces

annotation.surface: The title of a book or film, perhaps a black-and-white one.
annotation.walkthrough: All the King's Men is a novel and a film, and 'black and white' suggests old cinema; the king's men are really chess pieces, all of which together make a set.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the pieces, king's men in two colours, and all of them together make up the set.

blocks.note: Con = Conservative, the British political party
a fusion is a merger

annotation.surface: A merger of political parties ends in chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: disorder and bewilderment are what chaos amounts to.

indicators.note: swallowed up, so N is taken inside MUCH

blocks.note: much = lots; these are the outer letters
n is the algebraic symbol for an unknown number; it goes inside

annotation.surface: Someone eats a great deal, the quantity never measured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eat lots' reads as one instruction, but only 'Eat' is the definition; 'lots' is MUCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a manner attached: chewing steadily and audibly is a way to eat.

entries.clue: March, time on vacation: Apr is, unfortunately, coming in (7)

indicators.note: vacated, emptied, so TIME loses its middle and leaves T…E
things going badly, so the letters of APR IS fall out of order
the rearranged letters come into the emptied TIME

blocks.note: TIME emptied of its middle: the outer letters T and E
APRIS rearranged; it goes between T and E

annotation.surface: A diary entry: March, then holiday time, but April sadly arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'March' and 'Apr' plant the calendar, but March is a verb, to walk wearily; APR is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to walk wearily or trudge somewhere is to march, reluctantly.

entries.clue: Last of horses, except for grey (7)

indicators.note: the final letter of horses, S

blocks.note: last letter of horseS
unless = except if, except for

annotation.surface: The last horses left, apart from the grey one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grey' looks like a horse's colour, finishing the picture; it describes a dull, overcast day.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an overcast day with no sunshine looks grey.

indicators.note: in the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the last letters of witH nO cracklinG

annotation.surface: A pig roast that has ended up without any crackling.
annotation.walkthrough: Crackling is the crisp roasted pork skin, which suits a pig; here the words matter only for their last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is used especially of a castrated male pig reared for meat.

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: An old physician praises doctors for their foresight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' sits right beside 'medic' and looks like a plural noun; it is a verb meaning tampers with.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the Greek physician of the 5th century BC, father of medicine and namesake of the doctors' oath.

blocks.note: to pepper is to riddle, as with shot
in mint condition = perfect

annotation.surface: A puzzle about the ideal tangy taste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' reads as a puzzle, a noun; it is the verb, to pierce all over, as bullets pepper a target.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the mint oil used in sweets and toothpaste gives a sharp, cool taste.

entries.clue: Working out like that, learner in new routine (10)

indicators.note: SO and L go in the rearranged letters
made new, so the letters of ROUTINE take a fresh order

blocks.note: ROUTINE rearranged; these are the outer letters, split RE…UTION
so = like that, as in 'do it so'
L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A gym-goer's new exercise routine, learned just so.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all gym talk; 'Working out' is really the solving of a problem, and the whole word also nods at a New Year's resolution to exercise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the problem-solving sense: finding the answer is working it out.

entries.clue: Opening of sweeties for good kid (5)

indicators.note: the start of sweeties, its first letter S

blocks.note: first letter of Sweeties
pro = for, in favour of
G = good, the standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Opening a bag of sweets as a reward for a well-behaved child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word joining the pieces; it is PRO. Sprog is British slang for a child.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: British slang for a child.

entries.clue: How teams played, up to a point (8)

indicators.note: played about with, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A match report on how the teams played until one scored a point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up to a point' sounds like a scoreline; it means partly, to some extent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to some extent, partly, is the idiom 'up to a point'.

indicators.note: rejected, thrown back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: top = first, as in top of the class; this gets turned round

annotation.surface: Someone turns down the first prize.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First prize' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'prize' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trophy cup, or the pot of money in a card game, is a prize.

indicators.note: what the ears take in is the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: sent = launched, dispatched; say it and you hear the answer

annotation.surface: A new perfume is launched, pitched at the listener.
annotation.walkthrough: Perfume is for the nose, so 'for one's ears' jars on purpose: it tells you to hear the answer rather than smell it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fragrance worn on the skin is a perfume.

blocks.note: figuratively thrilling, like a charged atmosphere
the amplified kind, as opposed to acoustic

annotation.surface: A thrilling performance by guitar players.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash and the question mark mark the second half as a description, completing the phrase 'electric guitar'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: figuratively thrilling, as a charged atmosphere is, and literally amplified by electricity, as an instrument can be.

indicators.note: roaming off course, so the letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: The perfect moment to look at a wandering star, a planet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wandering star' is a planet, the literal Greek meaning, and pulls the eye skywards; the star is a film actor.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a handsome actor adored by fans, named for afternoon performances, is a star.

entries.clue: Sample first of steaming potato jackets (6)

indicators.note: the first letter of steaming, S
to jacket is to wrap, so TATER wraps round the S

blocks.note: tater, informal for potato; these are the outer letters
first letter of Steaming; it goes inside

annotation.surface: Trying a steaming-hot jacket potato.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jackets' reads as the potato skins, a noun; it is a verb, wraps, placing TATER round the S. A jacket potato is a baked potato in its skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small portion offered to try is a sample.

indicators.note: swallowed by, so the answer is inside the following words

blocks.note: inside scoundrEL Firewater

annotation.surface: A villain gulps down strong liquor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'firewater' both suggest hard liquor, which is the trap: the spirit is a supernatural sprite.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the little folklore creature is one kind of spirit.

indicators.note: drawing a line round, so FORGE goes round the A

blocks.note: to forge is to engineer, bring about; these are the outer letters
taken as it stands; it goes inside

annotation.surface: An engineer sketching the plan for a search.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person; it is a verb, to forge or contrive.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rummaging about, especially for food, is searching.

entries.clue: Clobber dressing fashionable set, outfit in claret and blue (4,3)

indicators.note: WHAM dresses, clothes, the rearranged letters by going round them
fashioned into a new shape, so SET is rearranged

blocks.note: to clobber is to hit hard, wham; these are the outer letters
SET rearranged; it goes after the W

annotation.surface: Fashion talk: clothes (clobber) dressing a stylish set in a claret-and-blue outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes, which suits the fashion surface, but here it is the verb, to hit. West Ham United is a London football club that plays in claret and blue.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the London football club plays in claret and blue, and 'outfit' means a team.

entries.clue: Disguise alter ego on the phone? (4)

indicators.note: heard down a phone line, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's alter ego in Stevenson's story

annotation.surface: Someone masks their other self when on a call.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disguise' and 'alter ego' both suggest a secret identity; the alter ego is the specific one, Mr Hyde.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: concealing something is a way of disguising it.

entries.clue: Turner has to put in something black after gold brushed over (7)

indicators.note: brushed back over itself, so OR is turned round
'put in' means inserted, so the word TO is placed inside TAR

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry; turned round it comes first
tar is black; these are the outer letters
taken as it stands; it goes inside

annotation.surface: The painter J M W Turner adds a dab of black after the gold is brushed over.
annotation.walkthrough: The Turner is a thing that turns, not the painter; 'after' puts TATOR behind the reversed gold.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: anything that spins or rotates something is a turner.

indicators.note: a piece taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: inside ephemeRA REmarkably

annotation.surface: A collector remarks on an unusual piece of ephemera.
annotation.walkthrough: Ephemera are collectable throwaway items like tickets, which suits 'rare' in a dealer's sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: seldom found means unusual.

blocks.note: per person, as tickets are priced per diner; two words in this sense
in the lead

annotation.surface: Everyone is in the lead.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration (5) hides that the first sense is two words, A HEAD, meaning per person.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: A HEAD, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per person; and in the lead means winning.

entries.clue: Moving swiftly past supposition, finally getting to the point (9)

indicators.note: the final letter of supposition, N
ARROWING comes after the N, going past it

blocks.note: last letter of suppositioN
arrowing = shooting along like an arrow

annotation.surface: A speaker skips past an assumption to reach the main point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting to the point' sounds like cutting to the chase in talk; it describes tapering to a tip.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: tapering to a tip is literally getting to a point.
